qns_content.text: In an aquatic ecosystem, the major producers are:

text_solutions: Phytoplankton are the primary producers in aquatic ecosystems, converting sunlight into energy through photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly defines net primary productivity (NPP)?

options.text: Total energy lost as heat in an ecosystem

text_solutions: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the energy available to consumers after subtracting respiration losses from Gross Primary Productivity (GPP).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of decomposers?

text_solutions: Decomposers do not perform photosynthesis; they break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the nitrogen cycle is incorrect?

options.text: Denitrification releases nitrogen gas back into the atmosphere
Plants can absorb nitrogen gas directly from the atmosphere
Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric nitrogen into usable forms
Decomposers help release nitrogen from organic matter

text_solutions: Plants cannot absorb nitrogen gas directly from the atmosphere; they depend on nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of decomposers in an ecosystem?

options.text: Breaking down organic matter into inorganic substances

text_solutions: Decomposers break down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic nutrients, making them available for uptake by producers.

qns_content.text: Which of the following ecosystems has the lowest net primary productivity?

text_solutions: Deserts have the lowest net primary productivity due to limited water availability and extreme climatic conditions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of a man-made ecosystem?

text_solutions: Forests are natural ecosystems, whereas crop fields, aquariums, and gardens are human-made ecosystems.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a producer in an aquatic ecosystem?

text_solutions: Phytoplankton are primary producers in aquatic ecosystems, performing photosynthesis to produce energy.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about biogeochemical cycles is incorrect?

options.text: They involve both living and non-living components
Nutrients are lost permanently from the ecosystem
Microorganisms play a role in nutrient cycling

text_solutions: Nutrients are not lost permanently; they are continuously recycled in ecosystems.

qns_content.text: Why is the detritus food chain important in a terrestrial ecosystem?

options.text: It reduces the number of primary consumers
It produces more energy than the grazing food chain

text_solutions: The detritus food chain plays a vital role in nutrient recycling by decomposing dead organic matter into usable forms.

qns_content.text: Which of the following best defines standing crop in an ecosystem?

options.text: Total biomass of living organisms in a given area at a given time
Total energy produced by an ecosystem per year
Total number of consumers in an ecosystem

text_solutions: Standing crop refers to the total biomass of living organisms in a particular trophic level at a given time.

qns_content.text: Which of the following ecological pyramids can NEVER be inverted?

text_solutions: The pyramid of energy is always upright because energy decreases at each trophic level due to heat loss.

qns_content.text: Which of the following represents a grazing food chain?

text_solutions: A grazing food chain begins with producers (plants) and moves up to herbivores (goat) and then to carnivores (man).

qns_content.text: What happens to most of the energy captured by producers in an ecosystem?

options.text: It is transferred completely to the next trophic level
It is lost as heat through respiration

text_solutions: Most of the energy captured by producers is lost as heat through respiration, following the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

qns_content.text: Which statement about energy flow in an ecosystem is correct?

text_solutions: Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional, moving from producers to consumers and eventually lost as heat.

qns_content.text: What is the role of decomposers in the nitrogen cycle?

options.text: They release nitrogen from organic matter into the soil

text_solutions: Decomposers release nitrogen from dead organisms and organic matter into the soil, making it available for plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about biological magnification is correct?

options.text: Toxic substances decrease at higher trophic levels
It occurs due to the accumulation of pollutants in organisms
Primary producers have the highest concentration of toxins
It has no effect on top predators

text_solutions: Biological magnification occurs when toxic substances accumulate in organisms and increase in concentration at higher trophic levels.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes the "10% Law" of energy transfer?

options.text: Only 10% of the energy is transferred to the next trophic level
All energy is transferred to the next trophic level
10% of energy is lost at each trophic level

text_solutions: According to the 10% Law, only 10% of the energy from one trophic level is transferred to the next, while the rest is lost as heat.

qns_content.text: Which of the following factors is responsible for the high productivity of estuarine ecosystems?

text_solutions: Estuarine ecosystems are highly productive due to abundant nutrients and sufficient sunlight for photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the best example of an autotrophic organism in an aquatic ecosystem?

text_solutions: Phytoplankton are autotrophic organisms in aquatic ecosystems that perform photosynthesis and serve as primary producers.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the primary reason for the low productivity of oceans?

text_solutions: Despite covering 70% of the Earth's surface, oceans have low productivity due to limited nutrient availability in deeper waters.

qns_content.text: What term describes the vertical distribution of different species in an ecosystem?

text_solutions: Stratification refers to the vertical arrangement of different species in an ecosystem, such as trees at the top, shrubs in the middle, and herbs at the bottom.

qns_content.text: Which process in decomposition results in the accumulation of a dark-colored organic substance in soil?

text_solutions: Humification leads to the accumulation of humus, a dark-colored organic substance in soil that improves fertility.

qns_content.text: Which of the following ecosystems has the highest net primary productivity?

text_solutions: Tropical rainforests have the highest net primary productivity due to high temperatures, abundant rainfall, and dense vegetation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a terrestrial ecosystem?

text_solutions: Forest is a terrestrial ecosystem, whereas ponds, lakes, and estuaries are aquatic ecosystems.

qns_content.text: Which type of ecosystem contributes the highest percentage to the Earth's total net primary productivity?

text_solutions: Tropical rainforests have the highest net primary productivity due to their high biodiversity, warm climate, and abundant rainfall.

qns_content.text: Which of the following describes the process of humification?

options.text: Conversion of organic matter into inorganic nutrients

text_solutions: Humification results in the accumulation of humus, a dark-colored organic substance in soil that improves fertility.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about ecosystem productivity is correct?

options.text: Gross primary productivity (GPP) is always less than net primary productivity (NPP)
NPP is the energy available to herbivores
NPP is not influenced by environmental factors

text_solutions: Net primary productivity (NPP) is the energy available to herbivores after subtracting respiration loss from GPP.

qns_content.text: Which type of ecological pyramid can be inverted in a pond ecosystem?

text_solutions: In an aquatic ecosystem, the pyramid of biomass is often inverted because the biomass of phytoplankton (producers) is lower than that of consumers.

qns_content.text: Which of the following best describes an ecological pyramid?

options.text: A diagram representing the number, biomass, or energy at each trophic level
A model showing the interdependence of organisms

text_solutions: Ecological pyramids represent the relative number, biomass, or energy of organisms at different trophic levels in an ecosystem.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about decomposers is correct?

options.text: Decomposers break down organic matter and recycle nutrients

text_solutions: Decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, break down dead organisms and recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.

text_solutions: Deer are herbivores that feed on grass and other plants, making them primary consumers in a grassland ecosystem.

qns_content.text: What is the correct sequence of decomposition processes?

text_solutions: Decomposition follows the sequence: Fragmentation (breaking into smaller particles), Leaching (dissolution of nutrients), Catabolism (breakdown by microbes), and Humification or Mineralization.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the best example of a self-sustaining ecosystem?

text_solutions: A forest is a self-sustaining ecosystem where biotic and abiotic components interact without human intervention.

qns_content.text: What is the role of decomposers in the ecosystem?

text_solutions: Decomposers break down organic matter and recycle essential nutrients back into the ecosystem, maintaining nutrient balance.

options.text: Total biomass produced by plants through photosynthesis
Total amount of energy lost as heat in an ecosystem

text_solutions: Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the total biomass or organic matter produced by plants through photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which factor determines the stratification of an ecosystem?

text_solutions: Stratification refers to the vertical distribution of different species in an ecosystem, such as trees forming the upper layer and shrubs forming the middle layer.

qns_content.text: Which process in an ecosystem is responsible for the release of nutrients into the soil?

text_solutions: Decomposition breaks down dead organic matter, releasing essential nutrients into the soil for plant uptake.
